title: Measuring RPS stringency
text: RPS state one row rules$rules (enactment first compliance year, target type, coverage share, design features, sources notes) one row per legal target rules$targets. States missing coding yet coded, get NA rather zero. Status. bundled coding covers 50 states DC. Rows marked verified = TRUE checked statute, DSIRE program page LBNL RPS & CES data, sources source notes columns. Single-number simplifications (one coverage share, one schedule states utility-specific targets) described notes. Please report corrections. can supply coding rps_rules(rules_path = ..., targets_path = ...).

title: Measuring RPS stringency
Measuring RPS stringency
text: Legal schedules often step (example Washington: 3% 2012, 9% 2016, 15% 2020). interpolation = "step" follows schedule exactly; "linear" (default) spreads ramp evenly target years.
code: lin  <- rps_stringency(2010:2022, "WA", method = "nominal") step <- rps_stringency(2010:2022, "WA", method = "nominal",                        interpolation = "step") plot(lin$year, lin$rps_nominal, type = "l", ylab = "Required share", xlab = "",      main = "Washington RPS") lines(step$year, step$rps_nominal, type = "s", lty = 2) legend("topleft", c("linear", "step"), lty = 1:2, bty = "n")

title: Measuring RPS stringency
code: cols <- c(CA = "#1b9e77", OR = "#d95f02", WA = "#7570b3", NC = "#e7298a",           MA = "#66a61e") plot(NA, xlim = c(2000, 2030), ylim = c(0, 0.65), xlab = "",      ylab = "Nominal requirement (share of sales)") for (st in names(cols)) {   d <- s[s$state == st, ]   lines(d$year, d$rps_nominal, col = cols[st], lwd = 2) } legend("topleft", names(cols), col = cols, lwd = 2, bty = "n")

title: Measuring RPS stringency
text: incremental measure subtracts state already produced enacted standard, separating new pressure existing renewables. build_panel() fills baseline EIA generation data: renewable share enactment year (first later year data), measured way target. New York, whose targets count existing hydro, baseline includes hydro (19% 2004, close 19.3% written RPS order); elsewhere non-hydro share. generation-based baseline weak guide states import electricity, Vermont. can always pass baseline: NA coverage-adjusted incremental values coverage share yet coded.
code: base <- data.frame(state = c("CA", "OR"), baseline_share = c(0.11, 0.03)) inc <- rps_stringency(c(2010, 2020, 2030), c("CA", "OR"),                       method = c("coverage_adjusted", "incremental"),                       baseline = base) inc #>   state year rps_coverage_adj rps_incremental rps_baseline_share #> 1    CA 2010          0.19700         0.08700               0.11 #> 2    CA 2020          0.32505         0.21505               0.11 #> 3    CA 2030          0.59100         0.48100               0.11 #> 4    OR 2010          0.00000         0.00000               0.03 #> 5    OR 2020          0.16160         0.13160               0.03 #> 6    OR 2030          0.28280         0.25280               0.03

title: Measuring RPS stringency
text: Texas Iowa set standards megawatts rather share sales. rps_stringency() converts , like Berkeley Lab , share covered sales capacity supply: MW x capacity factor x 8,760 hours / covered sales. capacity factor defaults 0.33 (typical wind) can changed. build_panel() supplies retail sales automatically; rps_stringency() pass :
code: tx_sales <- data.frame(state = "TX", year = c(2010, 2015),                        sales_gwh = c(358000, 380000)) rps_stringency(c(2010, 2015), "TX", method = "nominal", sales = tx_sales) #>   state year rps_nominal #> 1    TX 2010  0.04019296 #> 2    TX 2015  0.05909026 rps_stringency(c(2010, 2015), "TX", method = "nominal", sales = tx_sales,                capacity_factor = 0.4) #>   state year rps_nominal #> 1    TX 2010  0.04871874 #> 2    TX 2015  0.07162456

what: A template for Yin and Powers (2010)-style regressions
title: Measuring RPS stringency
text: Yin Powers (2010) regress non-hydro renewable share generation incremental requirement state year fixed effects. template shows workflow; replication, sample, coding controls differ bundled starter coding.
code: library(fixest) p <- build_panel(years = 2001:2022,                  vars = c("re_share_nonhydro", "rps_incremental",                           "rps_adoption", "gdp_real_pc",                           "elec_price_real")) feols(re_share_nonhydro ~ rps_incremental + log(gdp_real_pc) + elec_price_real |         state + year,       data = as_pdata(p, "fixest"), cluster = ~state)

title: rpspanel: US state energy-economy panels with RPS measures
text: rpspanel gives researchers documented, reproducible US state--year energy-economy panel (50 states + DC), Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) stringency measures, lines R. One call, one panel. build_panel() merges EIA energy use, prices production (SEDS), electricity generation retail sales, state CO2 emissions, BEA GDP, income population. Reproducible. Every variable’s source, vintage transformation recorded; codebook() cite_sources() document panel. Downloads cached vintages stay pinned. Better policy measures. rps_stringency() returns adoption, nominal, coverage-adjusted incremental (Yin Powers 2010) requirements, plus design-flexibility indicators. Fits existing tools. as_pdata() hands panel plm, fixest csdm; export_panel() writes CSV, Stata Parquet. Documentation: https://adebayomoses.github.io/rpspanel/

title: rpspanel: US state energy-economy panels with RPS measures
text: Studies US state energy policy affects growth emissions usually rebuild state--year dataset hand. Energy use prices come EIA, GDP population BEA, emissions EIA’s state CO2 data renewable policy rules DSIRE Berkeley Lab. source format, units, state codes release schedule, cleaning code rarely published. Renewable Portfolio Standards also often reduced yes/dummy, although real policies differ targets, timelines, coverage flexibility. rpspanel addresses problems: one function returns merged panel codebook vintage every source, rps_stringency() turns hand-coded, source-cited rules 50 states DC standardised annual stringency measures.

Python, PUDL project publishes machine-readable RPS clean energy standard data; rpspanel brings comparable policy measures R together economic energy variables needed panel analysis, hands result plm, fixest csdm rather re-implementing estimators.

title: rpspanel: US state energy-economy panels with RPS measures
text: National totals match published figures (2020: 4,570 million tonnes energy-related CO2, 4,010 TWh net generation, 331.6 million people):
code: snap <- as.data.frame(panel) snap <- snap[snap$year == 2022 & snap$state %in% c("CA", "TX", "NY", "IA", "WY", "VT"),              c("state", "co2_pc", "re_share_nonhydro", "gdp_real_pc",                "elec_price_real", "rps_nominal")] print(snap, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE) #>  state co2_pc re_share_nonhydro gdp_real_pc elec_price_real rps_nominal #>     CA   8.34            0.3438       80796           18.92      0.3850 #>     IA  22.33            0.6353       63181            8.11      0.0065 #>     NY   8.42            0.0658       89492           15.53      0.3622 #>     TX  22.01            0.2639       66566            8.61      0.0472 #>     VT   8.50            0.4733       54895           14.40      0.5900 #>     WY  96.58            0.2150       64183            6.98      0.0000 y20 <- panel[panel$year == 2020, ] c(co2_mt = sum(y20$co2_total), generation_twh = sum(y20$gen_total) / 1000,   population_m = sum(y20$population) / 1e6, real_gdp_tn = sum(y20$gdp_real) / 1e6) #>         co2_mt generation_twh   population_m    real_gdp_tn  #>      4571.9727      4009.7668       331.5781        20.1624 d <- as.data.frame(panel) d$group <- ifelse(d$rps_adoption %in% 1, "RPS in force", "No RPS") avg <- aggregate(re_share_nonhydro ~ year + group, data = d, FUN = mean)  par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 2.5, 1), las = 1) plot(NA, xlim = range(avg$year), ylim = c(0, max(avg$re_share_nonhydro) * 1.1),      xlab = "", ylab = "Non-hydro renewable share", main = "Renewable generation share, state average") cols <- c("RPS in force" = "#1b7837", "No RPS" = "#8c510a") for (g in names(cols)) {   s <- avg[avg$group == g, ]   lines(s$year, s$re_share_nonhydro, col = cols[g], lwd = 3) } legend("topleft", names(cols), col = cols, lwd = 3, bty = "n") w <- merge(d[d$year == 2005, c("state", "co2_pc")],            d[d$year == 2022, c("state", "co2_pc", "rps_nominal")],            by = "state", suffixes = c("_2005", "_2022")) w$change <- 100 * (w$co2_pc_2022 / w$co2_pc_2005 - 1)  par(mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 2.5, 1), las = 1) plot(w$rps_nominal, w$change, pch = 19, col = "#2166ac",      xlab = "Nominal RPS requirement, 2022 (share of sales)",      ylab = "Change in CO2 per capita, 2005-2022 (%)",      main = "CO2 per capita change vs RPS stringency") lab <- w$rps_nominal > 0 text(w$rps_nominal[lab], w$change[lab], w$state[lab], pos = 3, cex = 0.6, col = "grey30") abline(lm(change ~ rps_nominal, data = w), col = "#b2182b", lwd = 2)

Var.: log(co2_pc) #> Observations: 1,122 #> Fixed-effects: state: 51,  year: 22 #> Standard-errors: Clustered (state)  #>                   Estimate Std. Error   t value Pr(>|t|)     #> rps_nominal      -0.099899   0.142014 -0.703447 0.485040     #> log(gdp_real_pc)  0.194634   0.111038  1.752866 0.085755 .   #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #> RMSE: 0.065123     Adj. R2: 0.986657 #>                  Within R2: 0.027186 f <- file.path(tempdir(), "us_state_panel.dta") export_panel(panel, f)      # Stata file + us_state_panel_codebook.csv file.exists(f) #> [1] TRUE

title: rpspanel: US state energy-economy panels with RPS measures
text: RPS measures come coding bundled package, need API key:  Texas shows NA standard set megawatts. Passing retail sales (sales =), build_panel() automatically, converts Texas’s Iowa’s targets share covered sales. conversion assumes capacity factor (0.33 default, adjustable capacity_factor =), values approximate; agree Berkeley Lab’s equivalents within one percentage point every year. Use interpolation = "step" follow legal schedule exactly instead interpolating target years. See vignette("rps-stringency") five methods.
code: library(rpspanel) rps_stringency(c(2010, 2020, 2030), states = c("CA", "WA", "TX"),                method = c("adoption", "nominal")) #>   state year rps_adoption rps_nominal #> 1    CA 2010            1        0.20 #> 2    CA 2020            1        0.33 #> 3    CA 2030            1        0.60 #> 4    TX 2010            1          NA #> 5    TX 2020            1          NA #> 6    TX 2030            0        0.00 #> 7    WA 2010            1        0.00 #> 8    WA 2020            1        0.15 #> 9    WA 2030            1        0.15 s <- rps_stringency(2000:2035, states = c("CA", "NY", "OR", "IL", "NC", "WA"),                     method = "nominal") cols <- c(CA = "#1b9e77", NY = "#d95f02", OR = "#7570b3",           IL = "#e7298a", NC = "#66a61e", WA = "#e6ab02")  par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 2.5, 1), las = 1) plot(NA, xlim = c(2000, 2035), ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "",      ylab = "Required share of retail sales", main = "Nominal RPS requirements") for (st in names(cols)) {   x <- s[s$state == st, ]   lines(x$year, x$rps_nominal, col = cols[st], lwd = 2.5) } legend("topleft", names(cols), col = cols, lwd = 2.5, bty = "n", ncol = 2)

title: Annual RPS stringency indices — rps_stringency
text: years Years compute. states States include (default: 50 + DC). method One "adoption", "nominal", "coverage_adjusted", "incremental", "flexibility". rules rps_rules object; defaults bundled coding. baseline Optional data frame columns state baseline_share, existing (eligible) renewable share sales generation enactment. Overrides baseline_re_share rules. interpolation "linear" "step". adopt_from Year adoption 1: "enactment" "first_compliance". floor_zero TRUE, negative incremental requirements set 0. sales Optional data frame columns state, year sales_gwh (retail electricity sales, GWh, EIA's million kWh), used convert capacity-based standards shares. build_panel() supplies EIA retail sales. capacity_factor Assumed capacity factor resources meet capacity-based standard. default 0.33 typical wind, met Texas Iowa requirements.

title: Annual RPS stringency indices — rps_stringency
text: data frame state, year columns method: rps_adoption, rps_nominal, rps_coverage_adj, rps_incremental, rps_baseline_share, rps_oos_rec, rps_carveout, rps_acp.

title: Annual RPS stringency indices — rps_stringency
text: Methods: adoption: 1 RPS force year (adopt_from repeal), else 0. nominal: required renewable share retail sales year. Zero first compliance year. legal targets requirement interpolated linearly (interpolation = "linear") held last legal target ("step"); final target year held constant. first coded target lies enactment year, linear interpolation starts zero enactment. Capacity-based (MW) standards (Texas, Iowa) converted equivalent share covered sales: MW * capacity_factor * 8.76 / (sales_gwh * coverage_share), approach Berkeley Lab uses. needs sales; without NA. coverage_adjusted: nominal requirement times share retail sales covered standard. incremental: requirement beyond renewable share state already enactment, following Yin Powers (2010): nominal * coverage - baseline_share nominal requirement positive, otherwise 0. baseline taken baseline, baseline_re_share column rules. Also returns baseline used (rps_baseline_share). build_panel() measures baseline way target defined: including hydro states whose targets count existing hydro (baseline_includes_hydro = 1, New York), excluding otherwise. flexibility: indicators --state renewable credits, carve-outs alternative compliance payments, set 0 RPS force. States missing rule coding get NA every measure.

title: Annual RPS stringency indices — rps_stringency
text: Yin, H., & Powers, N. (2010). state renewable portfolio standards promote -state renewable generation? Energy Policy, 38(2), 1140-1149.

title: rpspanel 0.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-10-27 Initial version following project plan. Fetch layer: fetch_eia(), fetch_bea(), fetch_census() fetch_rps(), local download cache graceful failure service unavailable. Harmonise layer: harmonise_states(), deflate() convert_units(). Panel builder: build_panel(). RPS stringency module: rps_rules() rps_stringency() adoption, nominal, coverage_adjusted, incremental flexibility methods. Documentation helpers codebook() cite_sources(); output helpers as_pdata() export_panel(). bundled RPS rule coding (inst/extdata/) covers 50 states DC. 33 RPS states 6 voluntary-goal states verified statutes, DSIRE LBNL data (column verified), coverage shares filled , repeals coded (AZ 2026, KS 2015, MT 2021, OH 2027, TX 2025, WV 2015). Tested live EIA BEA APIs: BEA GDP tables now use current names (SAGDP9, SAGDP2), personal income labelled millions dollars, requests retry transient HTTP 500 errors EIA gateway. README now shows real output live run, figures man/figures/. fetch_census() now requires Census API key (API rejects keyless requests) tested live ACS 1-year data; output sorted state year, unit set default population variable. API responses web pages instead data (example rejected key) now raise clear rpspanel_http_error instead parse failure. API keys required data actually need downloading, cached panel can rebuilt offline without keys. Parquet export tested arrow (values column types round-trip unchanged). 12 original -RPS rows (AL, AK, AR, FL, GA, ID, KY, LA, MS, NE, TN, WY) now verified LBNL June 2026 data cite sources, 51 rows verified. Nebraska’s utility-adopted clean energy commitments (counted LBNL CES 2040) documented coded state RPS. rps_stringency() converts capacity-based (MW) standards (Texas, Iowa) share covered sales new sales capacity_factor arguments, following Berkeley Lab’s approach; build_panel() supplies retail sales automatically EIA key available, rps_nominal longer blank states. New optional rules column baseline_includes_hydro: incremental baseline now includes hydro New York, whose targets count existing hydro (2004 baseline 19%, matching 19.3% legal baseline). Fixed: single target force enactment (Iowa) longer breaks interpolation. Texas recoded 5,880 MW (2015) schedule binding; 10,000 MW 2025 figure non-binding goal (Berkeley Lab’s data). Converted Texas shares now match Berkeley Lab’s within 0.6 percentage points every year.
